entries.label: print
entries.name: print
entries.detail: Writes its arguments to stdout separated by **tabs**, with no trailing newline. Each is rendered as `tostring` would.

entries.label: println
entries.name: println
entries.detail: The same, with a trailing newline. This is the one to reach for.

entries.label: printf
entries.name: printf
entries.detail: Formats like [`String.format`](#string-format) and writes the result to stdout, with **no** trailing newline.

entries.label: tostring
entries.name: tostring
entries.detail: A readable rendering of any value. For a class instance implementing [`OpToString`](#prelude-interfaces) this calls its `toString()`; `print`, `println` and `..` all render the same way.

entries.label: type
entries.name: type
entries.detail: The runtime type name: `"integer"`, `"float"`, `"string"`, `"boolean"`, `"nil"`, `"function"`, `"table"`, or the class name for an instance.

entries.label: assert
entries.name: assert
entries.detail: If `v` is truthy, answers it with the nullability stripped. Otherwise throws `msg`, which defaults to `"assertion failed"`.

entries.label: error
entries.name: error
entries.detail: Raises `msg` as a runtime error, ending the program. Present for familiarity with Lua.

entries.label: String.byte
entries.name: byte
entries.detail: The Unicode codepoint of the `i`-th character, or `nil` when `i` is outside the string. `i` defaults to 1, so a bare `String.byte(s)` reads the first character.

entries.label: String.char
entries.name: char
entries.detail: Builds a string from codepoints. The inverse of `String.byte`.

entries.label: String.iter
entries.name: iter
entries.detail: A step closure over the characters of `s`, yielding each character and its 1-based index. Written for `for`, which stops when the closure answers `nil`.

entries.label: String.len
entries.name: len
entries.detail: The number of **characters**, which is not the number of bytes. `#s` is not defined for a string — use this, and use `#Bytes.fromString(s)` when the byte count is what you want.

entries.label: String.sub
entries.name: sub
entries.signature: String.sub(s: string, from: integer, to: integer?) -> string
entries.params: s: string, from: integer, to: integer?
entries.detail: The substring from `from` to `to`, both inclusive and 1-based. `to` defaults to the end of the string. Either index may be negative to count from the end, and both clamp, so an out-of-range slice is empty rather than an error.

entries.label: String.rep
entries.name: rep
entries.detail: `s` repeated `n` times, with nothing between the copies. `n` of zero or less gives the empty string.

entries.label: String.lower
entries.name: lower
entries.detail: Lowercases `s`. Unicode-aware, not ASCII-only: `Š` folds to `š` and `Ė` to `ė`, so this is correct for text in any language the string can hold.

entries.label: String.upper
entries.name: upper
entries.detail: Uppercases `s`, Unicode-aware in the same way as `String.lower`.

entries.label: String.find
entries.name: find
entries.signature: String.find(s: string, needle: string, from: integer?) -> (integer?, integer?)
entries.params: s: string, needle: string, from: integer?
entries.detail: The 1-based start and end indices of the first occurrence of `needle`, or `nil, nil` when there is none. `from` says where to start looking and defaults to 1.

entries.label: String.indexOf
entries.name: indexOf
entries.signature: String.indexOf(s: string, needle: string, from: integer?) -> integer?
entries.params: s: string, needle: string, from: integer?
entries.detail: The 1-based character index where `needle` first appears, or `nil` when it does not. `from` says where to start and defaults to 1.

entries.label: String.contains
entries.name: contains
entries.detail: Whether `needle` appears anywhere in `s`. An empty needle is always present.

entries.label: String.starts
entries.name: starts
entries.detail: Whether `s` begins with `prefix`. An empty prefix is always present.

entries.label: String.ends
entries.name: ends
entries.detail: Whether `s` ends with `suffix`. An empty suffix is always present.

entries.label: String.split
entries.name: split
entries.detail: Splits `s` on every occurrence of `sep`. The result always holds one more piece than there were separators, so splitting the empty string gives one empty piece rather than none. An empty `sep` splits into single characters.

entries.label: String.join
entries.name: join
entries.detail: Joins `parts` with `sep` between them, rendering each element the way `tostring` would. The same operation as [`Table.concat`](/saule/stdlib/table/#table-concat), with the arguments the other way round so the call reads as a sentence.

entries.label: String.trim
entries.name: trim
entries.detail: Removes whitespace from both ends. Unicode whitespace, not only the ASCII space — a non-breaking space goes too.

entries.label: String.trimStart
entries.name: trimStart
entries.detail: Removes whitespace from the start only.

entries.label: String.trimEnd
entries.name: trimEnd
entries.detail: Removes whitespace from the end only.

entries.label: String.replace
entries.name: replace
entries.signature: String.replace(s: string, from: string, to: string, limit: integer?) -> string
entries.params: s: string, from: string, to: string, limit: integer?
entries.detail: Replaces every occurrence of `from` with `to`, or only the first `limit` of them when `limit` is given. Literal text, not a pattern. An empty `from` matches nothing and returns `s` unchanged, so this can never loop forever.

entries.label: String.padStart
entries.name: padStart
entries.signature: String.padStart(s: string, width: integer, fill: string?) -> string
entries.params: s: string, width: integer, fill: string?
entries.detail: Pads `s` on the **left** until it is `width` characters long. `fill` defaults to a single space and repeats if it is longer than one character. Never truncates: a string already at or past `width` comes back unchanged.

entries.label: String.padEnd
entries.name: padEnd
entries.signature: String.padEnd(s: string, width: integer, fill: string?) -> string
entries.params: s: string, width: integer, fill: string?
entries.detail: The same, padding on the **right**.

entries.label: String.format
entries.name: format
entries.detail: C-style formatting. The specifiers are `%d` and `%i` (integer), `%f` and `%g` (float), `%s` (any value, rendered as `tostring` would), `%x` and `%X` (hexadecimal), `%o` (octal), `%c` (a character from a codepoint) and `%%` for a literal percent sign.

entries.label: Bytes.of
entries.name: of
entries.detail: Builds a buffer from byte values. The arguments are typed [`byte`](../README.md#the-byte-type), so a literal outside `0..=255` is a **compile** error rather than a runtime surprise, and a computed value has to narrow with `as byte` first.

entries.label: Bytes.empty
entries.name: empty
entries.detail: The empty buffer. Useful as a starting value for an accumulator, and as the fallback when a read returns nothing.

entries.label: Bytes.concat
entries.name: concat
entries.detail: Joins buffers in order. This is what `..` would do if it accepted `bytes` — it does not, because concatenation builds a string.

entries.label: Bytes.fromString
entries.name: fromString
entries.detail: The UTF-8 bytes of `s`. Always succeeds, because every Saule string is already valid UTF-8.

entries.label: Bytes.toString
entries.name: toString
entries.detail: The buffer as text, or `nil` when it is not valid UTF-8.

entries.label: Bytes.len
entries.name: len
entries.detail: The byte count. `#b` is the same thing, as a value you can pass around.

entries.label: Bytes.byte
entries.name: byte
entries.detail: The byte at `i`, or `nil` when `i` is outside the buffer. The result is a [`byte`](../README.md#the-byte-type), which is in `0..=255` by construction and widens to `integer` for free.

entries.label: Bytes.sub
entries.name: sub
entries.signature: Bytes.sub(b: bytes, from: integer, to: integer?) -> bytes
entries.params: b: bytes, from: integer, to: integer?
entries.detail: The slice from `from` to `to`, both inclusive and 1-based. `to` defaults to the end, negatives count from the end, and both ends clamp — so an out-of-range slice is empty rather than an error.

entries.label: Bytes.indexOf
entries.name: indexOf
entries.signature: Bytes.indexOf(b: bytes, needle: bytes, from: integer?) -> integer?
entries.params: b: bytes, needle: bytes, from: integer?
entries.detail: The 1-based position where `needle` first appears, or `nil` when it does not. `from` says where to start. An empty needle matches at `from`.

entries.label: Bytes.toHex
entries.name: toHex
entries.detail: Lowercase hexadecimal, two characters per byte.

entries.label: Bytes.fromHex
entries.name: fromHex
entries.detail: Parses hexadecimal back into a buffer. `nil` for an odd number of digits or any non-hex character, rather than a buffer that is quietly half right.

entries.label: Bytes.toArray
entries.name: toArray
entries.detail: The buffer as one element per byte. The expensive direction — every byte becomes a boxed table element — and explicit about it.

entries.label: Bytes.fromArray
entries.name: fromArray
entries.detail: Packs elements back into a buffer. `nil` when an element is out of range — which the typechecker prevents for a `byte[]`, but not for a table that arrived through `any`.

entries.label: Math.floor
entries.name: floor
entries.detail: Rounds toward negative infinity. An `integer` comes back unchanged.

entries.label: Math.ceil
entries.name: ceil
entries.detail: Rounds toward positive infinity.

entries.label: Math.round
entries.name: round
entries.detail: Rounds to the nearest integer, with a half rounding **away from zero** — `2.5` goes to `3` and `-2.5` to `-3`. This is not banker's rounding: a `.5` never rounds toward even.

entries.label: Math.sign
entries.name: sign
entries.detail: `-1`, `0` or `1`. Always an `integer`, whatever flavour went in.

entries.label: Math.type
entries.name: type
entries.detail: `"integer"` or `"float"` for a number, `nil` for anything else. The way to ask which flavour a value that arrived through `any` actually has.

entries.label: Math.abs
entries.name: abs
entries.detail: Magnitude, in the flavour it was given.

entries.label: Math.min
entries.name: min
entries.detail: The smallest of its arguments, which must all share one flavour.

entries.label: Math.max
entries.name: max
entries.detail: The largest of its arguments.

entries.label: Math.clamp
entries.name: clamp
entries.signature: Math.clamp<N>(n: N, lo: N, hi: N) -> N
entries.params: n: N, lo: N, hi: N
entries.detail: Pins `n` into the inclusive range `[lo, hi]`.

entries.label: Math.fmod
entries.name: fmod
entries.detail: The remainder after truncated division, in the flavour it was given. The sign follows the **left** operand, which is also what the `%` operator does — unlike Lua, where `%` floors and takes the sign of the right one.

entries.label: Math.modf
entries.name: modf
entries.detail: Splits a number into its integer and fractional parts, as a two-element table of floats.

entries.label: Math.pow
entries.name: pow
entries.detail: `a` raised to the power `b`. **Always a float**, which is what lets it answer a negative exponent — `2 ^ -1` is an error on integers, while `Math.pow(2, -1)` is `0.5`.

entries.label: Math.sqrt
entries.name: sqrt
entries.detail: The square root.

entries.label: Math.exp
entries.name: exp
entries.detail: `e` raised to the power `n`.

entries.label: Math.log
entries.name: log
entries.detail: The natural logarithm, or the logarithm in `base` when one is given.

entries.label: Math.sin
entries.name: sin
entries.detail: Sine of `n` **radians**.

entries.label: Math.cos
entries.name: cos
entries.detail: Cosine of `n` radians.

entries.label: Math.tan
entries.name: tan
entries.detail: Tangent of `n` radians.

entries.label: Math.asin
entries.name: asin
entries.detail: Arcsine, in radians. `n` outside `[-1, 1]` has no answer and gives `nan`.

entries.label: Math.acos
entries.name: acos
entries.detail: Arccosine, in radians.

entries.label: Math.atan
entries.name: atan
entries.detail: Arctangent, in radians. With one argument it is the arctangent of `y`; with two it is the `atan2` form — the angle to the point `(x, y)`, with the quadrant resolved correctly, which a single-argument arctangent cannot do.

entries.label: Math.deg
entries.name: deg
entries.detail: Radians to degrees.

entries.label: Math.rad
entries.name: rad
entries.detail: Degrees to radians.

entries.label: Math.random
entries.name: random
entries.detail: A uniform float in `[0, 1)` — zero is possible, one is not.

entries.label: Math.random
entries.name: random
entries.detail: A uniform integer in `[1, n]`, both ends included.

entries.label: Math.random
entries.name: random
entries.detail: A uniform integer in `[lo, hi]`, both ends included.

entries.label: Math.randomseed
entries.name: randomseed
entries.detail: Resets the generator, so a sequence of `Math.random` calls repeats exactly. This is what makes a test or a procedurally generated world reproducible.

entries.label: Math.ult
entries.name: ult
entries.detail: Compares two integers as **unsigned** 64-bit values. A negative integer has its top bit set, so it reads as a very large unsigned number.

entries.label: Table.insert
entries.name: insert
entries.signature: Table.insert<V>(t: table<V>, value: V, pos: integer?) -> nil
entries.params: t: table<V>, value: V, pos: integer?
entries.detail: Appends `value` to the end of the array part, or inserts it at `pos`, shifting everything from `pos` onward one place to the right.

entries.label: Table.remove
entries.name: remove
entries.detail: Removes and returns the last element, or the one at `pos`, shifting the rest left. `nil` when there is nothing to remove, which is what makes a table usable as a stack without a separate emptiness check.

entries.label: Table.sort
entries.name: sort
entries.signature: Table.sort<V>(t: table<V>, cmp: fn(V, V) -> boolean) -> nil
entries.params: t: table<V>, cmp: fn(V, V) -> boolean
entries.detail: Sorts the array part in place. `cmp(a, b)` answers `true` when `a` must come before `b`.

entries.label: Table.reverse
entries.name: reverse
entries.detail: Reverses the array part in place. [`Iter.reverse`](/saule/stdlib/iter/#iter-reverse) returns a new table instead.

entries.label: Table.clear
entries.name: clear
entries.detail: Removes every entry, array part and map part alike. The table itself stays the same table, so anything else holding a reference to it sees it empty.

entries.label: Table.len
entries.name: len
entries.detail: The array length — the same number `#t` gives, as a value you can pass around.

entries.label: Table.contains
entries.name: contains
entries.detail: Whether `value` appears in the array part. Compares with `==`, so a class implementing [`OpEq`](#prelude-interfaces) is matched by its own rule rather than by identity.

entries.label: Table.indexOf
entries.name: indexOf
entries.detail: The 1-based position of the first `==` match, or `nil`. For a **predicate** search, use [`Iter.findIndex`](/saule/stdlib/iter/#iter-findindex).

entries.label: Table.keys
entries.name: keys
entries.detail: Every key: the array indices `1..#t` in order, then the map's keys in no particular order.

entries.label: Table.values
entries.name: values
entries.detail: Every value, in the same order as `Table.keys`.

entries.label: Table.slice
entries.name: slice
entries.signature: Table.slice<V>(t: table<V>, from: integer, to: integer?) -> table<V>
entries.params: t: table<V>, from: integer, to: integer?
entries.detail: A **new** table over the 1-based range, `to` defaulting to the end. Negative indices count from the end, and an out-of-range slice is empty rather than an error.

entries.label: Table.copy
entries.name: copy
entries.detail: A shallow copy of both halves. Elements are **shared**, so copying a table of instances gives a new table pointing at the same instances.

entries.label: Table.concat
entries.name: concat
entries.signature: Table.concat<V>(t: table<V>, sep: string?, from: integer?, to: integer?) -> string
entries.params: t: table<V>, sep: string?, from: integer?, to: integer?
entries.detail: Joins the elements with `sep` between them, rendering each as `tostring` would. `sep` defaults to the empty string, and `from` / `to` restrict the range.

entries.label: Iter.collect
entries.name: collect
entries.detail: Drains a step closure until it answers `nil`, collecting what it produced. This is the bridge from anything iterable — a `String.iter`, a `File.lines`, a class implementing `Iterable` — into the rest of this module.

entries.label: Iter.map
entries.name: map
entries.signature: Iter.map<V, U>(t: table<V>, f: fn(V) -> U) -> table<U>
entries.detail: Applies `f` to every element, giving a new table of the results. The result type follows `f`'s return type, so mapping to a different type is ordinary.

entries.label: Iter.filter
entries.name: filter
entries.signature: Iter.filter<V>(t: table<V>, pred: fn(V) -> boolean) -> table<V>
entries.detail: Keeps the elements `pred` accepts, in their original order.

entries.label: Iter.reduce
entries.name: reduce
entries.signature: Iter.reduce<V, A>(t: table<V>, init: A, f: fn(A, V) -> A) -> A
entries.params: t: table<V>, init: A, f: fn(A, V) -> A
entries.detail: Folds left from `init`, threading an accumulator through every element. The accumulator may be any type, not only the element type.

entries.label: Iter.forEach
entries.name: forEach
entries.signature: Iter.forEach<V>(t: table<V>, f: fn(V) -> nil) -> nil
entries.detail: Runs `f` for its effect on every element and answers nothing. Use it when the point is the side effect; use `map` when the point is the result.

entries.label: Iter.find
entries.name: find
entries.signature: Iter.find<V>(t: table<V>, pred: fn(V) -> boolean) -> V?
entries.detail: The first element `pred` accepts, or `nil` when none does.

entries.label: Iter.findIndex
entries.name: findIndex
entries.signature: Iter.findIndex<V>(t: table<V>, pred: fn(V) -> boolean) -> integer?
entries.detail: The 1-based position of the first element `pred` accepts, or `nil`.

entries.label: Iter.any
entries.name: any
entries.signature: Iter.any<V>(t: table<V>, pred: fn(V) -> boolean) -> boolean
entries.detail: Whether **any** element matches. `false` for an empty table.

entries.label: Iter.all
entries.name: all
entries.signature: Iter.all<V>(t: table<V>, pred: fn(V) -> boolean) -> boolean
entries.detail: Whether **every** element matches. `true` for an empty table — there is no element that fails.

entries.label: Iter.count
entries.name: count
entries.signature: Iter.count<V>(t: table<V>, pred: fn(V) -> boolean) -> integer
entries.detail: How many elements match.

entries.label: Iter.take
entries.name: take
entries.detail: The first `n` elements, or all of them when there are fewer. Never an error.

entries.label: Iter.skip
entries.name: skip
entries.detail: Everything after the first `n` elements. Empty when `n` is at or past the length.

entries.label: Iter.first
entries.name: first
entries.detail: The first element, or `nil` when the table is empty.

entries.label: Iter.last
entries.name: last
entries.detail: The last element, or `nil` when the table is empty.

entries.label: Iter.chunk
entries.name: chunk
entries.detail: Fixed-size groups, in order. The last group is short when the length does not divide evenly.

entries.label: Iter.zipWith
entries.name: zipWith
entries.signature: Iter.zipWith<V, U, A>(a: table<V>, b: table<U>, f: fn(V, U) -> A) -> table<A>
entries.params: a: table<V>, b: table<U>, f: fn(V, U) -> A
entries.detail: Pairs the two tables up and combines each pair with `f`, stopping at the shorter one.

entries.label: Iter.flatten
entries.name: flatten
entries.detail: Concatenates the inner tables into one. **One level only** — nest the call to go deeper.

entries.label: Iter.reverse
entries.name: reverse
entries.detail: A **new** table in reverse order. [`Table.reverse`](/saule/stdlib/table/#table-reverse) reverses in place instead.

entries.label: Iter.unique
entries.name: unique
entries.detail: Drops later duplicates, keeping the first occurrence and the original order. Compares with `==`, so a class implementing [`OpEq`](#prelude-interfaces) is deduplicated by its own rule.

entries.label: Iter.sortBy
entries.name: sortBy
entries.signature: Iter.sortBy<V, K>(t: table<V>, key: fn(V) -> K) -> table<V>
entries.detail: A **new** table sorted ascending by the extracted key, using `<` — so a class implementing [`OpCompare`](#prelude-interfaces) sorts by its own rule. Stable: elements with equal keys keep their original order.

entries.label: Iter.groupBy
entries.name: groupBy
entries.signature: Iter.groupBy<V, K>(t: table<V>, key: fn(V) -> K) -> table<K, table<V>>
entries.detail: Buckets the elements by key. The key must be a `string`, `integer` or `boolean` — the types a table can be keyed by.

entries.label: Io.open
entries.name: open
entries.detail: Opens `path` and answers a handle, or `nil` when it cannot — the file is missing, the directory is not writable, the path is a directory.

entries.label: Io.lines
entries.name: lines
entries.detail: A step closure over the lines of `path`, written for `for`. With no argument it reads standard input instead.

entries.label: Io.read
entries.name: read
entries.detail: Reads from standard input in the given formats:

entries.label: Io.write
entries.name: write
entries.detail: Writes its arguments to standard output with nothing between them and no trailing newline. `Io.stdout.write(...)` is the same thing.

entries.label: read
entries.name: read
entries.detail: Reads from the handle in the same formats [`Io.read`](#io-read) takes — `"l"`, `"L"`, `"a"` and `"n"`. The result is a `string`, so this is for **text**: a file that is not valid UTF-8 needs `readBytes`, and so does a fixed number of bytes.

entries.label: readBytes
entries.name: readBytes
entries.detail: Reads raw [`bytes`](#bytes), assuming no encoding. With no argument it reads to end of file; with a `count` it reads up to that many and answers `nil` only at end of file — so a read loop terminates.

entries.label: write
entries.name: write
entries.detail: Appends text at the handle's current position. A `bytes` passed here would be rendered as `<bytes len=N>` — use `writeBytes`.

entries.label: writeBytes
entries.name: writeBytes
entries.detail: Appends the bytes themselves, with no encoding applied. Writing non-UTF-8 to stdout or stderr is an error rather than mojibake.

entries.label: lines
entries.name: lines
entries.detail: A step closure over the handle's remaining lines. The same as `Io.lines`, for a file you have already opened — which is what you want when the handle was opened in a particular mode, or when some of it has already been read.

entries.label: seek
entries.name: seek
entries.detail: Moves the read/write position and answers the new position, counted in bytes from the start. Defaults to `(IoSeek.Cur, 0)`, which moves nothing and so answers where you are.

entries.label: flush
entries.name: flush
entries.detail: Forces buffered writes out to the file. Writes are buffered, so another reader — a different handle, another process — does not see them until the buffer is flushed or the handle is closed.

entries.label: close
entries.name: close
entries.detail: Releases the handle, flushing whatever is buffered. Using a handle after closing it is an error, so close last.

entries.label: Os.time
entries.name: time
entries.detail: The current Unix epoch in **seconds**. Comparable across runs and across machines, which is what makes it the right thing to record.

entries.label: Os.timeMillis
entries.name: timeMillis
entries.detail: The same instant in **milliseconds** — the resolution needed to time a request, a frame or a test.

entries.label: Os.clock
entries.name: clock
entries.detail: Seconds from a **monotonic** clock: it never goes backwards, even if the system clock is adjusted, but its origin is arbitrary — only *differences* mean anything.

entries.label: Os.difftime
entries.name: difftime
entries.detail: `t2 - t1`. Present for familiarity with Lua; plain subtraction does the same thing here, because both arguments are already integers.

entries.label: Os.date
entries.name: date
entries.detail: Formats a Unix epoch using `strftime`-style specifiers. `format` defaults to `"%c"` and `time` to now.

entries.label: Os.parsedate
entries.name: parsedate
entries.detail: The inverse of `Os.date`: reads `text` and answers the Unix epoch, or `nil` when it does not match. `format` defaults to `"%Y-%m-%d"`.

entries.label: Os.sleep
entries.name: sleep
entries.detail: Pauses the whole program. Fractions are allowed, so sub-second waits are ordinary.

entries.label: Os.getenv
entries.name: getenv
entries.detail: The value of an environment variable, or `nil` when it is not set.

entries.label: Os.setenv
entries.name: setenv
entries.detail: Sets a variable **for this process** and anything it spawns afterwards. It does not reach the shell that started the program.

entries.label: Os.cwd
entries.name: cwd
entries.detail: The absolute path of the current working directory.

entries.label: Os.chdir
entries.name: chdir
entries.detail: Changes the working directory, answering `false` when it cannot — the path does not exist, or is not a directory.

entries.label: Os.exists
entries.name: exists
entries.detail: Whether anything exists at `path` — a file, a directory or a symlink.

entries.label: Os.list
entries.name: list
entries.detail: The names of a directory's children — names only, not full paths.

entries.label: Os.mkdir
entries.name: mkdir
entries.detail: Creates a directory, answering `false` when it cannot. With `recursive` set, it creates the missing parents too; without it, a missing parent is a failure.

entries.label: Os.remove
entries.name: remove
entries.detail: Removes a file, or an **empty** directory. `false` when it cannot — the path is missing, or the directory still has something in it.

entries.label: Os.rename
entries.name: rename
entries.detail: Moves or renames, answering `false` when it cannot. Within one filesystem this is atomic, which is what makes write-then-rename the safe way to replace a file.

entries.label: Os.tmpname
entries.name: tmpname
entries.detail: A path under the system temp directory that nothing is using yet. It is a **name**, not a file: nothing is created until you create it.

entries.label: Os.fsInfo
entries.name: fsInfo
entries.detail: Metadata for one path, or `nil` when nothing is there. `path` defaults to the current directory.

entries.label: Os.pid
entries.name: pid
entries.detail: This process's own process id.

entries.label: Os.args
entries.name: args
entries.detail: The command-line arguments passed to the script, without the interpreter or the script path.

entries.label: Os.execute
entries.name: execute
entries.detail: Runs `cmd` **through the shell** and answers its exit code. The child's output goes to this process's own stdout and stderr — nothing is captured.

entries.label: Os.capture
entries.name: capture
entries.detail: Runs `cmd` through the shell and captures it: the exit code, everything it wrote to stdout, and everything it wrote to stderr. Nothing reaches the terminal.

entries.label: Os.spawn
entries.name: spawn
entries.signature: Os.spawn(program: string, args: table<string>?, cwd: string?, env: table<string, string>?) -> Process?
entries.params: program: string, args: table<string>?, cwd: string?, env: table<string, string>?
entries.detail: Starts `program` and answers a handle **while it runs**, so the program can write to it, read what came back, and carry on in between. `nil` when it cannot be started.

entries.label: Os.exit
entries.name: exit
entries.detail: Ends the process immediately with `code`, which defaults to 0. Nothing after it runs.

entries.label: Os.platform
entries.name: platform
entries.detail: Which operating system this is, as an enum: `Linux`, `Macos`, `Windows` or `Other`, whose `.value` is `"linux"`, `"macos"`, `"windows"` or `"other"`.

entries.label: read
entries.name: read
entries.detail: Whatever has arrived on stdout, up to `max` bytes (64 KiB by default). **Never blocks**: an empty buffer means "nothing yet", which is not the same as "nothing more" — see [`p.atEof()`](#p-ateof).

entries.label: readErr
entries.name: readErr
entries.detail: The same, for stderr. The two streams are separate, so output written to one never appears in the other.

entries.label: write
entries.name: write
entries.detail: Writes to the child's stdin and answers how many bytes went in. An error once stdin has been closed.

entries.label: closeStdin
entries.name: closeStdin
entries.detail: Drops the child's stdin so it sees end of input. Idempotent — closing twice has expressed one intention.

entries.label: poll
entries.name: poll
entries.detail: The exit code if the child has finished, `nil` while it is still running. Remembered, so asking twice is fine.

entries.label: wait
entries.name: wait
entries.detail: Blocks until the child exits **and its output has arrived**, then answers its exit code. Closes stdin first — a child waiting for input and a parent waiting for the child is a deadlock, and this is the end that can tell.

entries.label: kill
entries.name: kill
entries.detail: Ends the child. `true` when the signal was delivered, `false` when it had already exited — which is not an error.

entries.label: running
entries.name: running
entries.detail: Whether the child is still going. Asks the operating system rather than trusting a flag, so it is accurate without a prior `poll`.

entries.label: pid
entries.name: pid
entries.detail: The child's process id.

entries.label: available
entries.name: available
entries.detail: How many bytes are waiting on stdout, without taking them — how far behind a reader is.

entries.label: atEof
entries.name: atEof
entries.detail: Whether stdout has **ended and been drained**. Both halves matter: a child can exit with output still sitting in the buffer, and reporting end of file then would lose it.

entries.label: Saule.atLeast
entries.name: atLeast
entries.detail: Whether this toolchain is `version` or newer. Compares dotted numeric components, so `"26.7"` satisfies `"26"` and `"26.7"` but not `"26.8"`.
